prs.title: Persist Hub artifact authority and deletion intents
prs.body:
Artifact namespaces need stable host ownership before a service restart or deletion can be reconciled. Add a private, bounded authority snapshot for installation identity, root namespaces, per-session principals and content-free deletion intents. Exact associations survive reopen; children share the root namespace while retaining separate principals.

The existing Hub lock owns the authority lifetime. Startup loads pending project deletions before constructing the lazy Supervisor with an immutable policy snapshot. Snapshot replacement uses actual file sync, rename and directory sync; a retained candidate blocks new authority until explicit durability reconciliation. All writes reject closed ownership. First creation and authority-less retries sync the full canonical parent chain, including partially created paths.

Real tests cover strict schema/private-path refusal, stable identity, root versus child deletion, file/directory failures and debt/close fencing. Owned service processes are killed after real SQLite ensure/tombstone commits but before acknowledgments, then restarted to prove one namespace, stable identity and no resurrection. A separate owned process runs actual Hub startup, is killed after the durable project-deletion record but before authority import, then restarts and proves the tombstone is imported.

Independent task and scoped reviews approved this authority slice after the durability and fault-coverage fixes. At `a65c970c299314bb2250e381394455e4a1ce8a2d`, focused parent-path tests passed (0.503s), matching race passed (1.515s), vet and pinned lint passed. The preceding package/owned-process/race results are recorded separately and retain their exact scopes. Both retry regressions failed before their fixes. Earlier first-round regressions were collected after implementation and are documented as such, not as test-first evidence.

This is the authority foundation, stacked on #1933. Private daemon transport, live lineage/lease/grant fences, Clear and production deletion hooks remain subsequent slices. A retained-session/project mismatch review item is explicitly carried into the lifecycle slice. No complete 100-agent, browser or A01–A22 acceptance is claimed. Assembly targets `codex/shared-artifacts-integration`; do not merge this work to main.

After assembling the reviewed runtime and authority at `5eeba11d371d535020cac5ca349e2b739204f7db`, `MODULES=. ROOT_FULL=1 WEB=0 scripts/gate/run-module-tests.sh -count=1` passed in 119.39s on Darwin arm64 / Go 1.27.0. This is the full root-module integration gate; agent, frontend, native and browser qualification retain their separately stated scopes.

External exact-head review disposition: the two lifecycle findings (actual project/session deletion hooks and child-specific grant revocation) are required in the next lifecycle slice and are not implemented by this foundation PR. The entropy-error claim does not apply to the pinned Go1.27 `crypto/rand.Read`, which fills or terminates and never returns an ignored error. Directory-sync errors intentionally fail closed; treating unsupported sync as success would violate the adopted durability requirement. Explicit durability reconciliation is provided for the owned coordinator. Two cleanup observations (unused directory-creation tracking and an unreachable ErrDeleted exception) are carried into the same-source lifecycle slice. The external review body is retained; its successful job status is not a clean-review claim.

prs.body:
A managed artifact call can be accepted remotely before its result reaches the transcript. Add an optional application-owned tool runtime and a durable session journal that retain the exact request and outcome until transcript settlement is durable. Recovery checks current permissions and retries the same invocation identity; it never reconstructs a mutation from model text.

Raw managed arguments are validated before generic JSON repair. One SDK-free MCP result carrier preserves host data independently of the limited provider projection. Bounded per-result persistence covers normal completion, cancellation and partial writes, including delegate and skill delivery obligations. Runtime bindings follow actual child construction and tool narrowing.

Compaction now commits one final marker with direct references to the canonical retained transcript occurrences. This preserves recovered assistant/result pairs across intervening accepted input, journal eviction, repeated compaction and reopen, without copying large host payloads. A whole retained-unsynced marker settles through the existing durability barrier before its narrow history/note/skill changes are published. Canonical summary inputs protect explicitly private tool data while normal model requests retain their live results. Model switching refuses before changing state when such a publication is pending.

prs.title: fix(agent): preserve an unchanged retirement timer deadline
prs.body:
Hold for a confirmed delayed timer-arm race. The current relative-clock interface cannot safely preserve the intended deadline across all measured clock-advance interleavings. An absolute-deadline constructor is proposed and awaits Jesse's architectural decision; this head is not merge-ready.

A redundant retirement evaluation can read the old clock time, then reset an already armed deadline after virtual time advances. The reset schedules the old remaining duration from the new time and postpones retirement; this caused the daemon regression in #1936 to miss its expected expiry.

The controller now remembers the absolute deadline it armed and skips resets for the same deadline. Disarm and consumed ticks clear that value, so genuine eligibility changes and retry paths still rearm. Clock and timer interfaces are unchanged.

A gated regression forces the stale-time interleaving, waits for the timer decision, and verifies the original expiry. Reverting only the production fix produces the duplicate-arm failure. Plain, race, and tagged timer tests; the exact daemon regression; normal/tagged/Windows vet; formatting; and scoped lint pass. Independent review and local RoboRev branch review2550 found no blocking findings.

Fixes #1936. The fix covers redundant resets; it does not change the relative timing semantics of initial or genuinely changed timer arms.

prs.title: Add a Hub-supervised shared artifact service
prs.body:
Agents and presentations need one artifact service owned by the Hub. This adds a lazily started child in the installed evener binary, authenticated MCP Streamable HTTP, and private AppWire bootstrap/control. Trusted filesystem traversal is checked before the service-held OS lock, which covers the store lifetime; parent loss drains and reaps the child, and restart restores namespace policy before issuing fresh grants.

The HTTP boundary accepts the selected MCP profile, rejects batches before SDK dispatch, and bounds admission and complete responses. Caller IDs are limited to a 1024-byte ID-only response envelope measured by the pinned SDK codec before dispatch, preserving the existing 2 MiB request and 16 MiB response limits. The phone's transcript footer reads the same turn-summed session usage totals the web details panel reads, with the same scope fallback, so both surfaces show the same session figure for a session with no thread-level cumulative usage (a fork child never gets one stamped, per `agent/fork.go`'s `writeForkChild`).

prs.title: fix(mobile): the conversation keeps its turns and wire cursor coherent across paging and rehydrate
prs.body:
Decomposed out of #1885 after five review rounds (Jesse's "five review rounds means decompose" rule). This PR is the state-layer mechanism only: `mobile/src/state/conversation.ts` and `mobile/src/services/conversation.ts`'s turn plumbing. #1885's footer half is B3a, stacked on this PR.

## What this closes

The store's own top-level `olderCursor` (a UI-only, intentionally capped "is there another page to fetch" signal, F8) and the conversation's own `ThreadModel.olderCursor` (the wire truth `sessionTokens` reads) are two different values that #1885's review kept finding collapsed into one at different sites, across five rounds:

- **loadOlder** derives `conversation.olderCursor` from the wire's own `nextCursor`, never the store's capped field (so the item cap stopping the UI's own paging never mislabels a partial sum as a full session).
- **rehydrate** preserves page-loaded turn history across a same-session reread: its own itemLimit-bounded window can't see turns loaded by an earlier `loadOlder`. Turn ownership is tracked separately from item ownership (`pageOwnedTurnIds`, alongside the existing `pageOwnedIds`), so a page whose display rows were all deduped or evicted still keeps its turns for the merge.
- **rehydrate's cursor** carries the prior conversation's own wire cursor only when the merge actually contributed a turn beyond the fresh read's own window - not whenever page history merely exists somewhere in the session's lifetime.
- **Both merges** (loadOlder's and rehydrate's) go through the package's own `mergeOlderItemPage` (`turnsMatch`/`mergePageTurn`) instead of an id-only filter: `thread/turns/list` is itself item-paginated, so a turn can be split into fragments across a page boundary, or two turns can be logically the same but carry different ids. The service now exposes the wire `ThreadTurnsListResponse` (`turnsPage`) from both `loadOlder` and `readProjection` so the store folds it through the package's real, identity-aware merge - never a second, hand-rolled one.

## Per-state table (a session with no thread-level cumulative usage, so sessionTokens is always summing turns)

| state | store cursor | conversation cursor | turns | scope |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| initial (open) | `null` (F8's live path establishes it separately) | `"cursor-1"` (from the hydrated model) | `[t2]` | `loaded` |
| loadOlder (wire has more) | `"cursor-2"` | `"cursor-2"` (= wire `nextCursor`) | `[t1, t2]` | `loaded` |
| cap hit (wire still has more) | `null` (F8 stops paging honestly) | `"more"` (unaffected by the cap) | `[t1, t2]` | `loaded` |
| rehydrate, page history kept, contributes beyond the fresh window | unchanged | prior conversation's own wire cursor | merged (identity-aware) | `loaded` |
| rehydrate, page history exists but the fresh window already covers it | unchanged | fresh read's own | fresh reread's own | per fresh read |
| rehydrate, no page history | fresh read's own | fresh read's own | fresh reread's own | per fresh read |

A test per row lives in `mobile/src/state/conversation.test.ts`'s two `describe` blocks ("D18 B3 round 5" and "D18 B3 round 6").

## Failing-first tests (watched fail against `origin/main`, pass with the fix)

- `merges the older page's turns into conversation.turns and advances conversation.olderCursor`
- `keeps conversation.olderCursor at the wire's cursor even when the item cap stops paging`
- `rehydrate preserves the older turns loaded via loadOlder`
- `cap hit then rehydrate: conversation.olderCursor stays the wire truth, not the store's capped null`
- `evicted/filtered page: a turn survives a rehydrate even when none of that page's items did`
- `a turn split across a page boundary keeps its usage instead of being dropped by an id-only filter`
- `rehydrate with page history but a fully-covering fresh window: scope follows the fresh read, not a stale accumulated cursor`
- `returns the older page's wire turns alongside items`

## Falsification

Reverted `mobile/src/services/conversation.ts` and `mobile/src/state/conversation.ts` alone to `origin/main`, ran `mobile/src/state/conversation.test.ts` and `mobile/src/services/conversation.test.ts`: 8 failed exactly as above. prs.title: fix(hub): a superseded endpoint save re-anchors the draft identity (#1250)
prs.body:
Fixes #1250

## Root cause

`InstanceSheet`'s pre-write replacement detector compares `draftIdentity(instance)` against `seededIdentity.current` before every save. `DRAFT_IDENTITY_FIELDS` includes the derived `endpointFingerprint`, which identifies the complete resolved endpoint even when `baseUrl` reads identically.

When a save that changes an endpoint-affecting field (`baseUrl`/`vars`/`protocol`/`surface`) is *superseded* by the store's own listing — a refresh that started after the save answers first, so the store discards the save's response — the listing already holds the change the save produced, and its derived fingerprint is the one the save produced. The seeded anchor, taken before the save, no longer matches. The next Save then compares like against unlike and refuses with:

> This instance was replaced under the same name; the form was reset to the instance now on screen.

Nothing was replaced: the draft and the listing agree on the endpoint; only the seeded identity anchor was stale.

## Change

`cmd/evener-hub/frontend/src/panes/settings/sections/credentials/InstanceSheet.tsx`

- Adds `supersededSaveLanded(instances, before, params)`: the entry the store's own listing carries for a plain (non-rename) superseded save, confirmed the same way `renamedInstanceLanded` confirms a rename — every identity field the save did not touch is carried over, and the derived `endpointFingerprint` is not compared as untouched when the save edited a field it derives from (`ENDPOINT_AFFECTING_FIELDS`). Returns `undefined` for renames and for a look-alike that differs on an untouched identity field.
- In `handleSave`'s superseded branch, when `supersededSaveLanded` returns the entry the save landed as, re-anchor `seededIdentity.current = draftIdentity(landed)` without reseeding, so the user's draft survives and the next Save compares like against like.
- Reads the store's listing once per save outcome instead of twice.

## Test evidence

Added to `InstanceSheet.test.tsx` (in the `describe("the form")` block):

`a superseded endpoint save re-anchors so the next save is not refused as a replacement`

It reproduces the issue's sequence: edit Base URL, save, let the refresh supersede the response with the landed listing (fingerprint `fp-before` → `fp-after`), then Save again. Confirmed RED without the source fix (the false `replaced under the same name` alert), GREEN with it.

```
npx vitest run --maxWorkers=4 --exclude "scripts/*.test.mjs" src/panes/settings/sections/credentials/InstanceSheet.test.tsx
# Test Files 1 passed (1); Tests 90 passed (90)
```

```
npx biome ci src/panes/settings/sections/credentials/InstanceSheet.tsx
# Checked 1 file. No fixes applied.
npx tsc --noEmit --incremental false   # exit 0
```

No test or guard was weakened; the retention/replacement suite (remove/recreate under the same name, fingerprint-only recreation, unkeyable replacement) is untouched and green.

prs.title: fix(web): Stop cancellation as durable outbox record state
prs.body:
## Summary

A Stop now writes its cancellation where the record it governs already lives: a durable `canceled` state on the IndexedDB mutation-outbox row, written at the user's click, before the stop action. This replaces the in-memory cancellation mechanisms whose races and reload hazards are enumerated in the design doc (`docs/design/stop-cancellation-outbox.md`, included in this PR).

Stacked on #1393 (`fix/stopped-session-recovery-ux`); retargets to `main` once that merges.

## Design decisions (ratified)

- **Placement**: a `canceled` record state — one authority per record, reopen-proof by construction in every tab and across reloads. No schema migration (whole-object puts; purely additive union member).
- **Timing**: the user's click is the cancel moment. `interrupt` cancels the ref's rows in the *same transaction* that enqueues the `turn/interrupt` record; `forceStop`/`shutdown` write first and abort — daemon untouched, retryable — if the write fails.
- **Scope**: all non-attempted rows for the ref. An attempted row may be on the wire; it is reported in-flight/uncertain, never claimed canceled.
- **Boundary (ratified 2026-09-18)**: when no mutation store exists at all (IndexedDB unavailable to the tab), there are no durable rows to protect, so forceStop/shutdown proceed; the abort applies only to a real store's failed write.

## Lifecycle of a canceled row

- Released only by an explicit user Retry (`canceled` → `submitting`); background retry modes cannot release it.
- Removed when the thread is cleared or the hub's deletion fence proves it gone. No TTL/GC.
- Surfaced in the QueueStrip's durable-rows slot with "Canceled by Stop" copy and the Retry affordance; note saves report in the note editor. Excluded from the in-flight chips and from Session's blocked-recovery notice (a canceled row is a settled fact, not a recovery obligation).
- `nextDispatchable` skips canceled heads (they provably never left the client) while staying FIFO-closed behind `blockedUnknown` heads — without this, a canceled head would park the very interrupt that canceled it.

## Tests

Real store, real flows, no mocks of the mechanism (spy-interleaved *real* cancel writes stage the race windows):

- interrupt cancels durably; discovery scans never resend; atomicity (aborted commit leaves neither interrupt nor cancellations)
- reload: fresh store connection + hydration leaves rows canceled
- cross-tab: tab B's reconciliation cannot resurrect tab A's cancellation
- post-resume: cancel → Resume → reconcile → no resend; Retry after Resume dispatches
- storage-failure aborts forceStop/shutdown before the RPC; no-store bypass proceeds
- dispatcher races: canceled between listing/re-read, between re-read/markAttempted; attempted-before-click settles normally; attempted + uncertain outcome classifies blockedUnknown, not canceled
- explicit Retry releases and dispatches; background modes don't; clear/delete removes canceled rows
- every wait-helper fails loudly

## Verification

- `make test-web` — full suite green (two unrelated load-flake failures during development — ConnectProviderDialog and ProviderConnection timeouts under host load — each rerun green in isolation; both files byte-identical to their pre-branch content or passing on the branch in isolation)
- `make test-api-package` — appwire-client qualification green (storage-port fixture gained `enqueueInterruptAndCancel`)
- Targeted vitest on every touched test file, red-first per unit
- `npx biome ci src ../../../appwire-client/typescript` clean

prs.title: fix(agent): decide the poisoned-transcript refusal inside the wake's claims (#1165)
prs.body:
Fixes #1165

## Root cause

`ProcessPendingUserInput` read one claimability snapshot (`wakeHasClaimableWork`, a `snapshot()` clone under `clientMutationStore.stateMu`), decided the poisoned-transcript refusal against it, and then claimed through `popQueueHead` / `claimSteeringCarrierInput`, which re-clone under a *different* mutex (`clientMutationStore.mu`) inside `mutate`. Nothing spanned the read and the claims, so a concurrent `InterruptClientMutation` (or a poisoning, or a queue/steering change) could land in between and make the two disagree:

- gate says work → hold arrives → claim takes nothing → one spurious `ErrWriterPoisoned` with nothing claimed (noise);
- gate says no work → hold released → `popQueueHead` takes a durable claim on a poisoned transcript, the case the guard exists to prevent: a turn is announced that then dies.

## Change

Each claim now decides the refusal on the same clone it acts on, and the wake reads the refusal from the claim instead of from a snapshot.

- `popQueueHeadRefusingPoison` (new) is the queue head's claim: after `queueHeadClaimable`, it returns `refuseBeforeClaimingOnPoisonedTranscript()` from inside the `mutate`, so the refusal is read on the generation the claim commits against and a refusal never commits anything. `popQueueHead` keeps its queue-mechanics signature and delegates to it, dropping the refusal (a refusal claims nothing and leaves the head queued; the wake and both drain-loop claim sites read the refusing form).
- `claimSteeringCarrierInput` returns its refusal the same way, so a poisoning or a Stop that lands after the caller decided the steer was runnable cannot hand it to a turn the transcript cannot record.
- `wakeHasClaimableWork` / `steeringCarrierClaimable` are removed: the wake no longer deep-clones the client-mutation journal per wake, and a wake that claims nothing stands down quietly instead of erroring.

Lock order is unchanged: the refusal reads the transcript's writer under `s.mu` while `mutate` holds `store.mu`, and no production path takes `s.mu` before `store.mu`.

## Test evidence

New tests in `agent/session_poisoned_wake_gate_test.go`, each confirmed failing on the pre-fix tree for the issue's own reason and passing after:

- `TestWakeRefusesTheSteeringCarrierWhenPoisonLandsBeforeTheClaim` — poisons inside the claim window via the existing `testOnly.steeringCarrierClaiming` seam. Pre-fix: `the refused wake announced turns [turn_m1]` (a turn announced that then dies). Post-fix: refused, no announcement, steering intact.
- `TestWakeStandsDownWhenAStopParksTheSteerBeforeTheClaim` — a Stop parks the rail in the same window. Pre-fix: spurious `ErrWriterPoisoned`. Post-fix: quiet stand-down.
- `TestPoisonedTranscriptRefusesTheQueueHeadClaim` — pre-fix `popQueueHead` claimed `"queued-behind-a-dead-transcript"` on a poisoned transcript; post-fix it refuses and the message stays queued.

Commands run on the rebased branch:

- `go build ./agent/...` — ok
- `go vet ./agent/` — ok
- `gofmt -l <changed files>` — clean
- `go test -count=1 -timeout 30m ./agent/` — `ok primeradiant.com/evener/agent 470.082s`
- `go test -race -count=1 -run 'TestPoisonedWriter|TestWake...|TestSteeringHeld|TestBufferedAcceptanceWake|...' ./agent/` — ok

## D6 piece 10: transcriptDisplayStore hub defaults + direct write

Stacked on #1844 (piece 9), base main per the queue's serial-merge convention.

Oracle: PR #1549 @dfde92160's transcriptDisplayStore.ts / transcriptDisplayStore.test.ts, for the read (hub defaults) and write (direct write) path specifically - the checkpointed draft editor half is out of scope (D6 piece 12).

### Size: over the ~400 non-test-line guideline, with a specific reason

`git diff --stat` for this PR's own commit: readyGenerationFence.ts +19, transcriptDisplayStore.ts +517 (345 code lines, 127 comment lines, 45 blank - counted with an awk pass, not just eyeballed). This is a genuinely new store, not an extraction like pieces 8/9, so it doesn't shrink the way those did. I kept the oracle's comment density (matching this codebase's established style of explaining WHY, not just WHAT) rather than trim it to hit the number. If you'd rather I cut this into two PRs after the fact (read path / write path), say so - I didn't split it because the plan's own item 10 names them as one unit ("hub defaults + the direct write") and splitting them now would require stubbing one half against the other with no real boundary to justify the seam.

### What's adopted directly from pieces 8/9 - zero re-derivation

- `createSettingsHubGeneration` (piece 8) for `beginReadyGeneration`/`endReadyGeneration` and the notification wiring.
- `retireSettingsHubPayload` (piece 8) for the in-flight-flags reset in `retirePayload`; the per-layout `patchTokens` reset (transcript-specific bookkeeping the shared fence knows nothing about) is layered on top by claiming a fresh `fence.claimWrite()` per layout before delegating, rather than trying to read `fence.writeToken` after the shared primitive's own internal `supersede()` - order-independent and correct either way a caller sequences it.
- `settleUnsettleableWrite` (piece 8) is **not used** here: I initially imported it, then found it (via `whyFenced`) is only ever called from the oracle's `saveDraft` (piece 12), never from `patchHubDefault` or `refreshFor`. Removed the unused import before pushing.
- Piece 9's `assertDraftDiscardable`/`persistCheckpointedDraft`/`discardCheckpointedDraft` are **not used** here either - discard/persist are checkpointed-editor-only concerns, entirely out of piece 10's scope.

### A real gap found in the shared fence, fixed here (additive, keybindings untouched)

The oracle's `readyGenerationFence.ts` (shipped inside #1549) has two members ours doesn't: `awaitingFirstPayload` / `firstPayloadApplied()`. keybindings' `retirePayload` resets `revision: 0` on every generation end, so nothing is ever "previous" going into a new generation and a hub restart's lower revision is never wrongly compared. Transcript's `hub` is deliberately **retained** across a transient disconnect (the effective configuration must not flap - `hub`'s own field doc says so), so its stale-guard needs an explicit "this generation has confirmed nothing yet, so the next payload is authoritative at any revision" escape hatch keybindings never needed. Added both members to the shared `ReadyGenerationFence` interface and implementation, TDD'd in `readyGenerationFence.test.ts` (2 new tests, watched fail with "awaitingFirstPayload is not a function" / `undefined`, then implemented). keybindingsStore.ts never reads or sets either member - confirmed by the full keybindingsStore.test.ts suite (90 tests) passing unchanged.

### Oracle hunks dropped as dead (piece 12's job, not lost - listed for whoever builds it)

- `restoreDraft`, `draftCheckpoint`, `staleDraft`, `invalidDraft`, the `discardStoredDraft` re-export - all draft-port-shaped, no port exists yet.
- `initialState()`'s `draft`/`storageUnavailable`/`draftUnreadable`/`draftConflict`/`draftError` fields and the `TranscriptDisplayStoreDeps.drafts` dependency.
- `applyHubDefault`'s draft-generation-stamping block (the `const draft = state.draft !== null && ... ? {...} : state.draft` dance) and its `draftConflict: staleDraft(draft, hub, fence.generation)` field - piece 10's `applyHubDefault` only publishes `hub`/preview-clearing/`extra`.

prs.body:
## D6 piece 9, part 2: checkpointed draft editor primitives

Stacked on #1841 (piece 8), base main per the queue's serial-merge convention - this PR's own commit is the last one (`git diff -M --stat origin/claude/sdk-d6-p8-settings-hub-generation...HEAD` below); the rest is p3-p8, already reviewed on their own PRs (#1808, #1791, #1792, #1841).

Oracle: PR #1549 @dfde92160's transcriptDisplayStore.ts, same caveat as #1841 - a second store not yet built, kept open only as a design check.

### What generalized, measured against the oracle

- `assertDiscardable`/`assertDraftDiscardable` - byte-identical body between both real stores (`fence.disposed || saving || writeUncertain || (storageUnavailable && !draftUnreadable)`). Fully extracted.
- `discardDraft`/`discardCheckpointedDraft` - the WHOLE body is identical once `restoreDraft` and the message string are parameters: gate, `discardClassified()`, adopt-a-replacement-via-restoreDraft on refusal, the five-field reset on success. Fully extracted.
- `persistDraft`/`persistCheckpointedDraft` - identical mint-id/save/catch shape, **with one real discrepancy** (below).

### What stays store-owned, and why

`editDraft`, `saveDraft`, `rebaseDraft` and the write-settle machinery (`settleWrite`/`settledWrite`) do not generalize cleanly:
- Transcript's draft carries a `layout` field a single-payload store has no equivalent of - one draft field can propose either layout, so "does this edit continue the existing draft" is a per-layout identity check (`existing?.layout === layout`) keybindings never needs. Unifying this needs the same kind of `Payload`-parameterized design piece 8 deferred for `setSupport`, not something to guess at in a `~400`-line extraction PR.
- The oracle predates keybindingsStore.ts's own `settleWrite` consolidation (this queue's D6-1808 simplify round, #1808 commits d13a216d9/162c49532): transcript's `saveDraft` still duplicates the settle-a-write logic inline rather than calling a shared `settleWrite`. It is not a fair comparison for what the CURRENT keybindingsStore.ts should generalize toward - piece 10 should compare against keybindingsStore.ts's post-simplify shape, not against #1549 as shipped, when it decides whether/how `settleWrite` generalizes.

### For whoever builds piece 10 (transcriptDisplayStore.ts) - the revision/appliedSerial/conflict finding from #1841 carries forward here too

#1841 found that `TranscriptDisplayStoreFields` in the oracle has no top-level `revision`, `appliedSerial` or `conflict` at all (a per-layout map instead), so those three don't belong in the generic core. The same is true one level up, for the draft's own identity: keybindings' `KeybindingsDraft.revision` is a single number; transcript's `TranscriptDraft` needs `layout` alongside `revision` to know WHICH per-layout revision it is stale against. Piece 10 should not assume a `Payload`/`Draft` type parameter can be bolted onto `createSettingsHubStore<Payload>` mechanically from these two pieces' primitives - `staleDraft`'s own signature already differs (`staleDraft(draft, confirmedRevision, currentGeneration)` for keybindings vs `staleDraft(draft, hub, currentGeneration)` in the oracle, reading `hub[draft.layout].revision` internally) - it needs a real design pass with both stores' actual code in hand, the same category of decision as `setSupport`.

### A real bug found and fixed along the way

`persistDraft`'s catch only set `storageUnavailable`, never `draftError` - the oracle's sets both. `nativePreferences.ts`'s `keybindingsDomain` projection reads `draftError` first, falling back to a hub-sourced message (`hubErrorMessage`) that says nothing about a local disk error. A user whose keybinding edit failed to persist locally (`editDraft`, `saveDraft` or `rebaseDraft` failing at the `persistDraft` step) saw `storageUnavailable: true` with **no error message at all** - `hubErrorMessage` returns `null` for this case (neither `loadError` nor `hubError` describe a draft-port failure).

Fixed by generalizing `persistCheckpointedDraft` to set both fields, matching the oracle. Pinned with a new test in keybindingsStore.test.ts (falsified: failed with `draftError: null` against the pre-fix code, paste below).

prs.title: fix(gate): pass the caller's build flags to the package enumeration (#1268)
prs.body:
Fixes #1268

## Root cause

The gate enumerated packages with a plain `go list ./...` and handed the result to `go test`. `go list` and `go test` do not see the same tree: `-tags` selects files, and `-race`, `-msan` and `-asan` each set a build tag of their own. A package whose only files sit behind `//go:build race` therefore exists for `make test-race` but not for the enumeration that decides what that run tests, so the package was silently never tested. Latent today (no such package in the tree), but a real divergence in the gate.

## Change

- New `evener-dev dev list-build-flags` subcommand (`cmd/evener-dev/listbuildflags.go`): prints, one per line, which of the caller's `go test` flags must also be given to the `go list` that enumerates the packages. It consumes each value with its flag first, so `-run -race` stays the regex it is, and it reuses the shard runner's value-flag tables for that.
- `scripts/gate/run-module-tests.sh` derives those flags once and passes them to both `go list` sites: the root module's package list and the agent module's subpackage enumeration.

## Test evidence

- `go test ./cmd/evener-dev/... -count=1` → `ok` (both packages)
- `go vet ./cmd/evener-dev/...` clean; `gofmt -l` clean; `bash -n scripts/gate/run-module-tests.sh` clean
- `TestPackageSelectionFlagsDecideWhatGoListCanSee` plants a tag-only package in a fixture module and shows it missing from plain `go list` and present once the forwarded flags are supplied. `TestPackageSelectionFlagsForwardsWhatChangesTheTree` covers the value-vs-flag cases (`-run -race`, `-ldflags -race`, `-args`).
- Independent check outside the test: in a fixture module with `//go:build race`, `go list ./...` → `racetagged/always`; `go list -race ./...` → `racetagged/always` + `racetagged/raceonly`.

Fixes #724

## Re-scope after #1819 landed

Rebasing onto current `main` collided with the sibling #1819, which had already
merged a #724 fix (Rebuild rescans when a mutation supersedes its unlocked scan,
bounded to 3 attempts) together with the incremental `publishFTS` (#725). That
rescan approach supersedes this branch's earlier merge/revalidation machinery, so
those commits are dropped; this PR now carries the #724 gaps `main` still has.

## Remaining fixes

`cmd/evener-hub/internal/hubcore/past.go`:

- **`foldOne` kept a stale indexed row.** A Rebuild can swap in the row it scanned
  (v1) after a Find probe already read a newer on-disk meta (v2); the old
  unconditional early return kept v1, so `All`/`Search` served the stale row and
  no `onChange` fired. `foldOne` now replaces the indexed row when the probe's
  meta is newer, using `metaNewer` (`UpdatedAt`, then `NameUpdatedAt` — a rename
  preserves `UpdatedAt` and stamps `NameUpdatedAt`).
- **`Find` returned the probe's meta** even when `foldOne` kept a strictly newer
  indexed row. `Find` now re-reads the cache after folding and returns the live
  row.

## Tests

Registered in `FuzzHubcoreScenarios`; each fails on the pre-fix path:

- `fuzzScenarioPastIndex_FoldReplacesStalerIndexedRow` — probe v2 over scanned v1.
- `fuzzScenarioPastIndex_FoldReplacesStalerIndexedRowOnRename` — rename-only v2
  (same `UpdatedAt`, newer `NameUpdatedAt`).
- `fuzzScenarioPastIndex_FindReturnsLiveRowAfterFold` — a concurrent writer
  indexes a newer row between Find's cache lookup and `foldOne`.

The prior review's "session resurrection via concurrent rebuild merge" findings
concern this branch's now-removed merge path; `main` has no merge (a superseded
scan rescans instead), so a deletion racing an edit/fold cannot be resurrected by

prs.title: fix(repair): explain a oneOf nested inside a property schema (#624)
prs.body:
## Root cause

`oneOfConstraintMessage` in `agent/internal/tool/repair/explain.go` only rendered a **root-level** combinator's branches. When a `oneOf` is nested inside a property's schema (`properties.opts.oneOf`), the failing cause's instance location is the container property (`/opts`), so `ExplainSchemaError` took the present-field path and emitted the generic:

```
tool: argument "opts" has the wrong type or value.
```

The real constraint — `opts` must satisfy one of the branches — was never surfaced. The caller (`agent/session_tool_repair.go`) also reduced the deepest cause's `KeywordLocation` to its last segment (`offendingKeyword`), discarding the `/properties/opts/oneOf/0/...` prefix that names the enclosing combinator.

Confirmed against santhosh-tekuri/jsonschema v5.3.1 for the issue's exact schema and args:

```
deepest instance="/opts" keyword="/properties/opts/oneOf/0/required"
offendingField="opts" offendingKeyword="required"
```

## Change

- `agent/session_tool_repair.go`: `offendingKeyword` -> `offendingKeywordLocation`, returning the full `KeywordLocation` path instead of just its last segment. `ExplainSchemaError` now receives `properties/opts/oneOf/0/required`.
- `agent/internal/tool/repair/explain.go`:
  - Derives the failing keyword as the last path segment (a bare keyword is a single-segment path, so existing callers/tests are unaffected).
  - Adds `enclosingOneOf`, which walks the keyword location (`properties/<name>`, `items`, `additionalProperties`, `propertyNames`, `oneOf`) to the schema node holding the innermost oneOf, only after descending at least one step so a root-level oneOf is never blamed on a property.
  - Adds `nestedOneOfMessage`/`branchConstraintMessage`/`scopedBranchExample`, rendering the branches against the property:

```
my_tool: argument "opts" violates a conditional rule on the combination of its properties (the schema's oneOf constraint), not the argument's own type or value.
Branch 0 requires: send all of "x".
Branch 1 requires: send all of "y".
Example: {"opts": {"x": "..."}}
```

  - A present field whose keyword location names no oneOf (e.g. `properties/opts/minProperties`) keeps the existing generic message — no unrelated combinator is attributed.
  - Root-level behavior is unchanged (verified by the existing #618/#625 tests).

## Test evidence

- `go test ./agent/internal/tool/repair/ -count=1` -> `ok` (includes the new `explain_oneof_nested_test.go`: nested oneOf names branches; leading-slash location; direct constraint wins over an unrelated oneOf).
- `go test ./agent/ -run 'PrepareToolCall_NestedOneOfNamesConstraint' -v` -> PASS — end-to-end through the real validator and `prepareToolCall`; asserts the error is not "wrong type or value" and names `opts`, `x`, and `y`.
- `go vet ./agent/ ./agent/internal/tool/repair/` -> clean; `gofmt -l` -> clean.

Fixes #624

prs.title: fix(agent): read branch-level enum constraints from their combinator arm (#622)
prs.body:
Fixes #622

## Root cause

`constraintMessage` resolved the failing field's schema with
`schemaProps(containerSchema)[field]` — always the top-level `properties` map.
`resolveSchemaErrorContainer` walks the *instance* location and cannot follow
combinator branches, so when the deepest cause was a branch-level enum such as
`/oneOf/0/properties/sandbox/enum`, the renderer read the same-named top-level
`sandbox.enum`. In the issue's reproduction the top-level enum allows `"off"`
while the oneOf arm forbids it, producing a self-contradictory message:

    delegate: argument "sandbox" is not one of the allowed values: "off", "read-only", "workspace-write", "restricted". Value is "off".

Only the deepest cause's *last* keyword segment reached the renderer
(`offendingKeyword`), so the branch path was discarded before it could be used.

## Change

- `offendingKeyword` → `offendingKeywordLocation` (`agent/session_tool_repair.go`):
  returns the deepest cause's full `KeywordLocation` (`oneOf/0/properties/sandbox/enum`)
  instead of only its final segment.
- `ExplainSchemaError` now takes that location and derives the keyword name from
  its last segment (a bare keyword name is a single-segment location, so callers
  without a path are unchanged).
- New `keywordParentSchema`/`constraintFieldSchema` (`explain.go`) walk the
  location's leading path — `properties/<name>`, `items`, `oneOf`/`anyOf`/`allOf`
  branch indices, `not`, `$defs`/`definitions` — into the root schema and resolve
  the field's own schema from the branch that actually carries the constraint.
  An empty or unwalkable location falls back to the container's `properties`
  map, preserving the flat behavior.

After the fix the reproduction renders:

    delegate: argument "sandbox" is not one of the allowed values: "read-only", "workspace-write", "restricted". Value is "off".

## Test evidence

- `agent/internal/tool/repair/explain_oneof_test.go`:
  - `TestExplainSchemaError_BranchEnumUsesBranchAllowedValues` — arms swapped so
    the deepest cause is the branch enum; asserts the exact branch-rendered
    message. Fails before the fix with the top-level list (`"off"` included).
  - `TestExplainSchemaError_BareKeywordStillReadsContainerEnum` — bare-keyword
    fallback still reads the container enum.
- `agent/session_tool_repair_issue622_test.go`:
  `TestOffendingKeywordLocationBranchEnum` — compiles the issue schema,
  validates, asserts `offendingField`/`offendingKeywordLocation`, and checks the
  end-to-end `ExplainSchemaError` output.
- Commands run:
  - `go test ./agent/internal/tool/repair/... -count=1` → ok
  - `go test ./agent/ -run 'Issue622|TestPrepareToolCall|TestExplainSchemaError|OneOf' -count=1` → ok
  - `go vet ./agent/internal/tool/repair/...` → clean
  - `gofmt -l <changed files>` → clean

prs.title: D6 piece 7: a keybindings draft carries its own ready generation
prs.body:
## D6 piece 7: a keybindings draft carries its own ready generation

Plan item 7 of the D6 decomposition (`.superpowers/sdd/2026-09-12-mobile-landing-queue-cont/d6-split-plan.md`): "A draft's generation is stamped by its first authoritative payload." Stacks on #1791 (p6).

### Mechanism (adapted from #1549's `10eba05a2`/`dc381b3f5`/`351dc2c6e`)
- `KeybindingsDraft` (local type, distinct from the wire-shaped `KeybindingsOverrides` also used for confirmed hub state and this store's write-path return values): `{ version: 1; revision: number; rules: KeybindingsRule[]; generation: number | null }`.
- `currentGeneration()` helper: `fence.generation >= 0 ? fence.generation : null`.
- `staleDraft`'s third param (`currentGeneration: number`, i.e. `fence.generation`): a non-null generation mismatch is stale regardless of revision, since hub revision numbering restarts on a hub replacement (reconnect to a different hub, or the same hub after a restart) and a coincidentally-identical revision must not read as current.
- Every draft construction site (`restoreDraft`, `editDraft`, `saveDraft`, `rebaseDraft`) stamps `generation: currentGeneration()`.
- `applyHubOverrides` stamps a `generation: null` draft with the live generation as part of accepting the first authoritative payload after it, before judging staleness for that same payload - closing the case where a draft restored before any generation began (a store built synchronously, before the host connects) never gets its generation check activated. Guarded on `fence.generation >= 0` (no call site here reaches this before `beginReadyGeneration` wires the fence, but kept the same shape defensively rather than relying on that staying true).

### Oracle tests
- `a draft restored before any generation began is stamped by the first authoritative payload, so a later hub replacement at the same revision is caught`
- `a draft is flagged stale across a generation change even when the new generation happens to report the same revision`
- Restored `generation: 1` (or `generation: null` for the pre-ready-restore case) to every existing draft-equality assertion the new field now touches (7 sites, not just the 2 the brief named - measured via a full test run after adding the field: `git diff` shows the affected lines).
- Added `draftConflictAfterSettle` to the settle-scenarios table (`saveDraft's post-reply sequence`): a settle that crosses a ready-generation boundary (fenced out by the generation ending, or by support dropping and returning - both begin a new generation) never trusts the draft's revision against it, even though the checkpoint itself settled cleanly.

### Falsification
Reverted only `keybindingsStore.ts` to #1791's head and re-ran `keybindingsStore.test.ts`: 10 failures (the two new tests plus 8 assertions expecting `generation`/`draftConflictAfterSettle` behavior the reverted file doesn't have). Restored with `git apply`; `git status` clean before committing.

prs.body:
## Slice 1: host registry + Connect state (component 08a-minimal)

First iterative build slice from the agreed requirements. Implements exactly the three user requirements — all from the UI with no file edit or restart — reusing the shipped seams (#1603/#1606): `hostreg`, `app_host_admin`, `app_host_attach`, `ChannelIfAttached`/`RemoteHostClientIfAttached`/`RemoteHostHandshake`, the spawn picker + Connect trigger.

### What was built (per requirement)

1. **Add a host from the UI (name + SSH address + key) and see it listed with status.**
   - `evener/host/add` (params `{name, address, keyPath?}`, result `HostRow`): validates exactly like hub.toml loading (component-03 rules via `hostreg`), refuses duplicates of live hub.toml/sidecar names with `InvalidParams`, persists UI-added entries to a `0600` sidecar (`hub.hosts.json` beside the selected hub.toml, atomic temp+fsync+rename) and registers a `RemoteHubSource` for the new name.
   - `evener/host/list` (params `{}`, result `{hosts: HostRow[]}`) + `evener/host/status` (params `{name}`, result `{host: HostRow}`): rows carry the effective entry (name/address/keyPath/origin) plus live state — `attached` via the `RemoteHostOnline` signal, handshake identity + preflight facts via the attached-only lookups. Never dials.
   - Frontend `Hosts` settings section (`panes/settings/sections/hosts.*` + `stores/hosts.ts`, registered in `sections.ts`/`Settings.tsx`): list rows with online/offline/connecting chips, add dialog (name/address/key), Connect button, remove with confirm.
2. **Connect to a host explicitly and see truthful online/offline state with retry.**
   - Reuses the shipped `evener/host/attach` unchanged (no new dial path). The Hosts section's Connect drives the same `evener/host/attach` the spawn picker uses; failure toasts the typed error and the row keeps its Connect button (retry affordance). Online-signal-but-channel-gone renders offline rather than a fact-less online row.
   - Add/remove invalidate the manifest's `sources` so the picker converges without waiting for the refresh tick.
3. **Remove a host cleanly; re-add works.**
   - `evener/host/remove` (params `{name}`, result `{host: HostRow(removed)}`): sidecar entries only (hub.toml names refused with "edit the file"), unknown names `InvalidParams`. Detaches via new `sshconn.Manager.DetachHost` (stops supervisor, drops channel, pairs Detached), removes the source + registry entry + sidecar row, persists. Removed stays removed (reload does not resurrect — pinned by test); re-add accepts the name fresh.
   - `hostreg.Registry.Remove` added (deletes host + edges, re-add starts clean).

### Explicitly deferred (with slice numbers)

- Slice 2: deploy/update/restart execution, tokens/gates/operation store/cursors/compensation, `evener/host/plan|deploy|restart|operations|update`, confirmation tokens.
- Slice 3: crash-fencing epochs, orphan-resolve, quarantine, `evener/host/orphan-resolve`, boot reaping.
- Slice 4: helper-gate install/migration (`handler-absent` path).
- Spec crash-window machinery (§5/§6: staged-receipt phase arms, stash-and-compensate, ubiquitous pre-handler reconcile, exact cap numbers, per-host gates, mutation receipts/idempotency keys, tombstone retained-row projections, generation/incarnation pairing, fingerprint live-reconciliation). Crash-safety by the simplest means instead: atomic sidecar writes + hub.toml-authoritative refuse/shadow rules + never-dial reads.

### Gate evidence

- `go build ./...` — exit 0.
- `go vet` on `appwire`, `cmd/evener-hub`, `hostreg`, `sshconn` — exit 0.
- `go test ./appwire/ ./cmd/evener-hub/internal/hostreg/ ./cmd/evener-hub/internal/sshconn/` — ok (incl. 6 new `TestRemove*`, 6 `TestDetachHost*`, 15 `TestHostManage*`/`TestHostSidecar*`).
- `go test ./cmd/evener-hub/ -run 'TestHostManage|TestHostSidecar|TestHostAdminAllowList|TestHubRPCRegistersExpectedHandlerSet|TestHubRouterMatchesCatalog'` — ok.
- Full `go test ./cmd/evener-hub/ -count=1` — first run caught 2 sibling-table failures (`TestHostAdminAllowListMatchesCatalog` missing allow/deny rows, `TestHubRPCRegistersExpectedHandlerSet` missing handler names); both fixed in the second commit, focused re-runs green. Full-suite re-run pending in CI.
- `make lint-generated` — PASS on the pushed head.
- `make test-web` — full gate was still running at report time; targeted runs green (`hosts.test.tsx` 6/6, `sections.test.ts` 14/14, Settings shell 41/41). Full result pending in CI.
- Failing-first: `TestHubRouterMatchesCatalog` failed with the 4 new catalog entries before `registerHostManageHandlers` landed, green after.

### Simpler-than-spec choices (with section references)

- No `mutationId`/`expectedGeneration` idempotency keys (spec "Contract / interfaces" add/update/remove shapes): single hub operator over a local socket re-listing after each mutation; deferred to slice 2's operation store.
- No `generation`/`incarnationId`/generation-scoped last-known store (spec "Protocol types" HostRow + "Data flow"): rows render live-or-offline; deferred to slice 3 fencing.
- No `update` method, no `teardown-retry`/`teardown-recover`, no `removed:true` tombstone rows in list (spec "Host mutations"): remove deletes outright; re-add is the recovery path.
- `HostRow` is a flat struct (no `RemovedRow` union arm, no `outcome` discriminator): the generator emits plain interfaces; union-shaped responses arrive with slice 2 if needed.
- Sidecar is JSON (`hub.hosts.json`), not TOML: hub.toml stays hand-authored and untouched; the sidecar merges after it with hub.toml-authoritative collision drops.
- Key path is sidecar-only (`keyPath`), not part of `hostreg.Host`/HostConfig: the registry mirrors hub.toml's `[[hosts]]` schema, which has no key field (SSH resolves keys via agent/ssh_config; explicit per-host keys are dial configuration).

Piece D of the #1580 decomposition plan (see the [decomposition plan comment](https://github.com/prime-radiant-inc/evener/pull/1580#issuecomment-5723104182)). **Stacked on #1737 (piece C)** — targets `main`, will be refreshed onto `main` after C lands.

## Summary
- Cut from #1580 (`53bb2b6ca`): `conversation.ts`, `conversation.test.ts`, and `mobile-native/src/liveImages.test.ts` (the live-image test suite this cutover also changes behavior for).
- The cutover-plus-deletions and the page-history layer are accepted at this size deliberately, per the plan comment: `main`'s `conversation.ts` already stages this as an explicit "Dual-write until c-2b" comment (folds into the package model AND runs the old row appliers, side by side, specifically so this cutover could land as one atomic step later) — that comment IS the flag, so a second, separate runtime flag on top of it would be redundant scaffolding. The page-history layer (`attachToSources`/`supersededBy`/`withPageHistory`/`retainedPageRow`/`capItems`'s orphan-trim) can't be split from the cutover either: `main` already supports `loadOlder` pagination against the row-applier world, and once rows come from `projectConversation` alone (which only re-derives the *current* live window), an older page loaded via `loadOlder` has nothing to reattach itself to on the next publish without this layer — shipping the cutover without it would regress pagination outright (this is exactly what round 3 and round 6 of #1580 itself already rediscovered after an earlier cut dropped it).
- Fixes this round's Low: `retainedPageRow`'s doc comment cited `project.ts`'s `clusterActivities` for identity/label/detail/state rules that piece C's `clusterActivityRun` now actually implements (`clusterActivities` itself just calls it, kept for `main`'s row appliers per piece C). Corrected the citation.

## A seam this branch did NOT cut cleanly at first, and how it's resolved
`conversation.test.ts`'s "shares one `askQuestionsByCall` scan between `projectConversation` and `pendingQuestions`" test called `pendingQuestions` (`mobile-native/src/questionAnswers.ts`, piece E's file) through `conversation.ts`'s own store. That's a real cross-piece dependency, not a D/E-independence violation in substance: the property under test — `liveAsksFor`'s memoization — lives entirely in `project.ts`'s `asksByTurns` (piece C, already `WeakMap`-keyed on `model.turns`), and `pendingQuestions` merely calls it. Removed the test from `conversation.test.ts` (it needed none of this piece's own cutover logic) and re-added it directly against `projectConversation`/`liveAsksFor` in piece E's `questionAnswers.test.ts`, where `pendingQuestions` itself lives — no file is shared between D and E's own diffs.

prs.title: fix(native): a collision-resistant, memoized identity for a question set
prs.body:
Piece E of the #1580 decomposition plan (see the [decomposition plan comment](https://github.com/prime-radiant-inc/evener/pull/1580#issuecomment-5723104182)). **Stacked on #1737 (piece C)** — targets `main`, will be refreshed onto `main` after C lands.

## Summary
- Cut from #1580 (`53bb2b6ca`, which already includes the original round-20 `questionsIdentity` fix): `questionAnswers.ts`, `QuestionSheet.tsx`, `screens.tsx`.
- Fixes both of today's new Mediums, found by RoboRev reviewing that round-20 fix itself:
  1. **Collision**: `questionsIdentity` hashed a *bounded* (truncated) copy of each question's canonical fields, so two questions sharing a prefix past the display bound (`MAX_ITEM_BYTES`) collided on the same identity.
  2. **O(payload) per render**: every render/keystroke rehashed the whole payload from scratch, even when the question-array reference (the one `reconcileBatches.ts` hands back unchanged when nothing changed) had not moved.
- Fix: hash the canonical fields directly with `cyrb53` (a fixed-size, collision-resistant, non-cryptographic hash — two 32-bit lanes mixed in one pass, no dependency) instead of truncating first, and memoize by question-array reference in a `WeakMap` so an unaffected render never rehashes at all.

## Test plan
- `npx vitest run --config mobile-native/vitest.config.mts mobile-native/src/questionAnswers.test.ts mobile-native/src/questionBatches.test.ts mobile-native/src/draftRepository.test.ts mobile/src/state/conversation.test.ts mobile/src/conversation/project.test.ts` — 494/494 pass. Two new tests measure the fix directly: a collision test (two oversized questions sharing a `MAX_ITEM_BYTES`-scale prefix now get distinct identities — RED against the pre-fix code) and a memoization test (200 repeated calls with the same array reference stay within 10x a single fresh computation — RED against the pre-fix code, which took >2s for the equivalent case before this test's numbers were dialed down for CI).
- `npm run check` (mobile-native tsc) — clean
