prs.title: refactor(native): rows are a projection of the model (D23c-2b)
prs.body:
Slice c-2b of SDK-migration row D23 (docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-12-sdk-migration.md), after c-2a (#1547, `d3c537e45`). The display rows become a projection of the package model: after every accepted frame the store publishes `capAndTruncate(projectConversation(applied))`, so a frame and a snapshot produce rows through the one projector and there is nothing for a row applier to disagree with.

## What the store does now

```ts
const applied = applyThreadNotification(state.conversation, n);
if (applied !== state.conversation) {
  set({ conversation: capAndTruncate(withPageHistory(state.conversation, projectConversation(applied))) });
}
// evener/thread/resync stays the authoritative refresh path; an item frame the
// reducer has no case for leaves the model untouched and asks for the canonical read.
```

The Q10 caps are one pure post-projection pass (`capAndTruncate` = `capItems` 500 rows, then `truncateItem` at 64 KiB with the marker). Because the bound is re-applied to whatever text a row carries, the truncation freeze is unnecessary: an oversized stream shows the same bounded prefix however much more arrives, and an authoritative short version is short again.

**Deleted from `mobile/src/state/conversation.ts`** (~1,200 lines): `projectSingleItem`, `decorateLifecycleItem`, `containingTurnStatus`, the cluster splicing (`findActivityTargetBy`/`findActivityTarget`/`findActivityTargetByIdentity`, `activityClusterSegments`, `mergeLiveActivityMembers`, `projectActivityMembers`, `replaceActivityTargetDetail`, `attachToSources`, `itemsAbsentFromSnapshot`), all seven row appliers with `publishModel`, `liveOwnedRevs`/`markLiveOwned`/`liveRevisionForItem`/`isLiveOwned`, `truncatedItemIds` with `truncateAndRecord`/`truncateAndRecordSingle`/`reconcileTruncationFrom`/`exceedsByteLimit`/`exceedsActivityDetailLimit`, the rehydrate live-ownership merge, and `getTruncatedItemIds` (interface + impl).

**Kept for D23d:** `pageOwnedIds` and the page prepend. The older pages live outside the model until D23d moves them in, so `withPageHistory` carries page-owned rows across every publish (and the rehydrate merge keeps the page's own cursor). `pruneEvictedIds` now prunes page ownership only.

**`mobile/src/conversation/project.ts`:** a `warning` item projects as the failure card its notice is (the reducer's `case "warning"` stamps `ItemModel.warning`); a reasoning row reads the per-`summaryIndex` chunks the model keeps (`joinedReasoningParagraphs`' rule, the same string[][] the web's think block renders); a question row on screen counts as a pending ask, so a live ask is answerable without waiting for a snapshot. `isActiveItem`, `activityState` and `clusterActivities` are private again, and `projectItemAttachments` with `inlineImageSrc`/`inputImage`/`outputImage` is deleted — the reducer resolves image sources now.

## Decision-2 behaviour deltas (what changes on the phone)

| Frame | Before (row appliers) | Now (projection of the model) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `item/agentMessage/reset` | blanked the row's markdown | removes the item, so the row goes; the restart streams from the `item/started` that follows |
| a delta naming no item in the model | requested a reread | ignored; the snapshot cut settles it |
| `item/toolOutput/delta` | required stored+incoming `callId` to match | routed by item id, as the wire routes it; the row keeps showing its own `callId` |
| a reasoning delta at a tool row (and the mirror) | requested a reread | invisible — the field it writes is not the field that row displays — and asks for nothing |
| `warning` with no active turn | appended a failure row | dropped (warnings are not transcript-persisted, so no snapshot would carry it) |
| ask_user `item/started`/`item/completed`, an unknown item type, a userMessage while an ask is pending | requested a reread | settled locally: tool row, question row + `askPending`, user row |
| a sparse assistant `item/completed` | re-projected the row from the sparse frame, blanking streamed text | keeps the streamed text (the model merged it) |

prs.title: transcript,agent: the fold names its retained entries by Seq (piece A2 of the #1100 split, closes #1200)
prs.body:
Piece A2 of the #1100 split (rebuilt on the transcript's durable `Entry.Seq` after #1281 was closed). **Closes #1200.**

## The bug (#1200)

After a fold, live history keeps the retained tail verbatim, but a restart resumed only the fold's SUMMARY. `ResumeHistory` anchored on the last CHECKPOINT/SUMMARY marker and discarded every entry before it, while the retained tail's entries sit *before* that marker. The old machinery (`persistedAppendLog` → `rewriteTail`) re-appended only the turns recorded *during* the fold, after the markers — never the preserved recent tail — so the tail vanished on restart.

## The fix

The fold now writes ONE durable `FOLD_RECORD` entry — a manifest naming, by transcript `Seq`, exactly the entries its published history is made of:

- `Layers`: the head marker's Seq (the summary, or the checkpoint when summarization did not run).
- `RetainedSeqs`: the pre-existing turns the fold kept (preserved tail + during-fold merge-back + injected steering), in history order.

The record is written last, after the markers and steering, so everything after it is live post-fold history. On restart, `ResumeHistory` finds the last fold record and rebuilds `[Layers entries] ++ [RetainedSeqs entries] ++ [entries after the record]`, each looked up by Seq. Because `recordTurn` already writes the *persisted* form as the entry and stamps the live turn's Seq to it, naming an entry by Seq yields the identical persisted content the old `rewriteTail` re-appended — without any duplicate entry.

Deleted wholesale: `persistedAppendLog`, `logPairPersistedLocked`, `persistedAppendLogBase`, `rewriteTail` (the fold's `snapAppends` snapshot bookkeeping goes with them).

New/changed:
- `schema.Turn.Seq int` (`json:"-"`, in-memory only): the durable per-line id, stamped at append or seeded from the entry on restore.
- `schema.FoldRecord` + `schema.TurnFoldRecord`; `Turn.Fold *FoldRecord` (`json:"fold_record,omitempty"`).
- `transcript.Writer` `Append`/`AppendDurable`/`AppendSynced` and the session write helpers now return the spent Seq.
- `ResumeHistory`/`resumeHistoryIndexed` reconstruct from the fold record; a pre-A2 transcript (marker, no record) falls back to the legacy last-marker anchor so an in-flight session's first restart after the upgrade does not suddenly replay its long-discarded prefix.
- Fork-provenance in `session_init.go` is decided per turn: `inheritedProvenanceTurns` maps `DivergenceTurn` through each resumed turn's own origin entry (and through the repair insertions), because a fold interleaves provenance — its own head marker, the parent turns it retained, its own tail — which no single boundary index can express. Byte-identical to the old contiguous-window math for the non-fold-record paths.

The `FOLD_RECORD` is never added to `Session.history`: `expandHistory` never sees it, and the reload projector emits no item for it (`default` case), so no projector shape change.

## Old-reader break — option 1, MEASURED (needs Jesse's ruling before merge)

Built under option 1 (no backward-compat machinery). `Turn.Fold` is a new wire field, so `decodeStrictJSON`'s `DisallowUnknownFields` (kata wf7e) makes a transcript that carries a fold record **unreadable to a pre-A2 daemon**. Measured with the exact strict decode against a `schema.Turn` that lacks the field:

```
A2 fold-record entry on the wire:
{"kind":"entry","seq":7,"turn":{"kind":"FOLD_RECORD","message":{"role":"","content":null},"timestamp":"0001-01-01T00:00:00Z","usage":{"input_tokens":0,"output_tokens":0,"total_tokens":0},"fold_record":{"fold_id":"3","layers":[5],"retained_seqs":[2,3,4]}}}

pre-A2 reader rejection: json: unknown field "fold_record"
```

Every reader (thread/read, resume, fork, doctor) decodes the whole transcript in one pass and aborts on the first error, so ONE fold-record entry makes the **entire transcript unreadable** to a pre-A2 build — not just that turn. It is clean (a decode error, no crash) and self-healing: the same daemon restarted on this build declares the field and reads the file fine. This is the same one-way door every prior `schema.Turn` field addition opened. Option 2 (an ignore-list format) cannot fix daemons already shipped — they do not know the field either — so it would only help future readers, which option 1 already covers by restart. **Holding for Jesse's explicit ruling on the compat break.**

## Live-Seq threading — the count

The returned-Seq stamp threads through **3 write choke points** (`writeTranscriptLocked` / `writeTranscriptDurableLocked` / `writeTranscriptSyncedLocked`) and the history-append helpers that already hold the Seq in hand (`appendTurnAfterTranscriptWrite(Locked)`, `recordTurn`, `appendPairedTurnVia`, `attachTranscript`, `appendClientMutationTranscriptLocked`, `appendUserInputTurnRefusingPoison`, the skill-reload reminder append). The stamp lives only in those helpers; the rest is the mechanical `(int, error)` signature change fanning out to call sites: **16 production files** and **~59 test files**, uniform and behavior-preserving.

## Gates

gofmt (toolchain binary), `go vet` ×3 both modules (incl. `GOOS=windows -tags evenerfuzz`), golangci-lint (0 issues, both modules), transcript + full agent suites, fold/resume/compaction suites, `-race -count=3` on the fold/resume/compaction/durability suites, apptranscript + appprojector + TUI suites. `/simplify` run (one dedup: an `appendEntry` closure in `resumeTurns`). No trailers.

prs.title: fix(web): keep stopped sessions usable through recovery
prs.body:
## Scope

A stopped session must stay usable, and recovering it must be explicit.

- The composer and its draft stay available for a stopped session, with the recovery notice and the Resume action, instead of the session collapsing into an unusable state. A recovery-fenced session whose snapshot still advertises `send: true` renders a **disabled** Send, not an actionable button that can only produce a refusal toast.
- Explicit Resume resumes the session, reports progress, and reports errors. It keeps its Stop fence: a Stop acknowledged while Resume is reconnecting sends no resume RPC, and a stale post-Resume read does not publish over a newer Stop. Stop generations are now baselined before the resume starts, so a Stop recorded against the resumed identity during the reconnect window cancels the resume rather than becoming the fence’s own baseline.
- Explicit Retry of a blocked mutation works and reports accurate outcomes, including the settled-elsewhere case: a retry whose target is viable is unaffected, and a record whose session is live elsewhere is reported as such rather than as a generic failure or a silent success (closes #1567).
- A background shared-note save that another connection settled now reports a distinguishable retained-draft status instead of appearing to have saved (closes #1568).
- The AppWire `FakeClient.resumeThread` runs its `beforeRequest` hook in the same order the real client does, so a test can no longer stage a Stop that the guard had already passed. The real client's `beforeRequest` throw path is now covered directly: a throwing fence sends no resume RPC, releases the pending resume, and leaves the reconnected primary healthy.

## What this PR deliberately does not do

An earlier revision of this branch made **Send implicitly resume a stopped session**. That feature has been removed from this PR and will land separately. (The review history: RoboRev's finding count on the full-scope branch went 4, then 4, then 3, then 8, and several of the newest findings were about that revision's own fixes.)

A later revision added **Stop cancellation of pending outbox sends**: an in-memory `canceledMutationIds` set, recorded after the Stop RPC, that reconciliation consulted before reopening a `blockedUnknown` record. **That mechanism has been moved out of this PR entirely.** RoboRev's review of it (both High findings and Mediums 4/5/6 on the previous head) converged on one root cause: the cancellation fact lived in per-tab memory while the IndexedDB outbox it governs is durable and shared across tabs, so every race and every reload/cross-tab gap was an artifact of that mismatch. The fix is not a better in-memory mechanism; it is a durable `canceled` state on the outbox record itself, written at user intent before the stop action. That design is written up separately and lands as a follow-up PR with its own review.

Two consequences, stated plainly:

- **Stop does NOT cancel pending outbox sends in this PR — the same behavior as `main` today.** A send that was in flight or blocked when the user stopped a session may still be delivered or retried by the outbox's normal lifecycle, exactly as before this branch. The follow-up PR is where Stop takes pending sends back.
- The mechanism's requester-protected invariant test — **"a Stop canceled retry is not resent by a later discovery scan"** — is removed with the mechanism, **sanctioned by the descope, and returns in the follow-up PR** wired to the durable design (its test plan keeps that invariant as test #1). Four sibling tests of the same machinery went with it: "a Stop during the retry's reconciliation is not overtaken by its dispatch", "a background-note retry does not release a sibling mutation canceled by the same Stop", "an explicit user retry after a Stop dispatches the canceled mutation", and "a Stop acknowledged after a hydration reopened a record puts it back to blockedUnknown".

What stays is the shell those findings also touched, now covering its own seams: the resume fence (`userIntentStopGenerations`, `resumeStopFence`, the client `beforeRequest` hook, the post-await re-check, the Session.tsx identity fence), the fenced-session notice with disabled Send and explicit Resume, the retry settled-elsewhere reporting, and the retained-draft note status. Stop-generation entries are now pruned when a ref's last holder releases it, so the fence map stays bounded by live refs.

## Final round on the d7d4c62 findings (2 Medium; Lows filed)

- **Stop-generation counter recycled by `releaseThread` (was Medium):** Stop generations now come from one page-wide monotonic sequence (`++userIntentStopSequence` per ref), so releasing a ref and re-ensuring it can never recycle a value a fence captured; pruning stays safe because values are forever-unique. Red-first: the reviewer's release/re-Stop race, plus the pruning test now covers delete-then-reincrement.
- **`retryBlockedMutation` returned `true` for an absent record (was Medium):** the background-note path no longer treats the retry's boolean as the settlement authority. After any retry it reads the ref's own records: absent means settled-elsewhere status (the #1568 status), still blocked means the draft's status was already true, and present in another state updates the draft from that actual state. The public boolean signature is unchanged.
- The three Lows are filed, not fixed here: **#1721** (pinned-ref generation leak), **#1722** (redundant projection refresh), **#1723** (hardcoded read-index test).

## Round on the fee4eb8 findings (4 Medium; Lows filed)

- **Note lookup ignored optimistic records (was Medium):** the persistence read now includes the optimistic store; an accepted-but-unreflected note reads pending until canonical state arrives, never settled-elsewhere (`97ddbf7c4`).
- **Recovery fence only covered `notLoaded` (was Medium):** an obligated local target is now fenced in EVERY non-active status, including a live `idle` snapshot with `resumeRequired: true`; the active carve-out is justified in the comment (`544198b51`). Red-first: live fenced idle renders a disabled Send, no turn/start enqueued.
- **Pre-RPC window fenced only the old ref (was Medium):** `resumeStopBaseline` gained a no-ref form that fires when ANY generation increased; `beforeRequest` uses it, so any acknowledged Stop suppresses the resume RPC (`9a27c4f8a`).
- **Release could delete the only Stop evidence (was Medium):** Stop generations now persist for the page session; pruning is reverted, and the replacement test pins the reviewer's exact interleaving (baseline absent-as-0, Stop, release, fence still throws) plus the global baseline's contract (`1585412ce`). This changes #1721's premise; noted on the issue.
- **Our own test-staging Low:** the existing test is renamed for the RPC-in-flight window it actually stages; the true reconnect window is covered by the new global-baseline tests (`a9c3494ca`, `3fa51902b`).
- Lows filed: **#1727** (`followUpEngaged` scoping). `settleAfterRead(9)` was already **#1723**.

## Simplify-code pass (quality only; requested after the Mediums rounds)

Four read-only angle reviews over the full PR diff, deduped to nine findings, applied under a no-behavior-change rule (helpers added, call sites delegate; zero test-file edits; revert-not-fix-forward on any gate failure).

- **Applied (7):** `resumeStopFence` delegates to `resumeStopBaseline`'s per-ref compare (doc comment corrected; the export stays for tests); the note draft's record-to-status mapping is shared with `refreshPersistence`; `beforeRequest` takes the baseline directly; one `retryErrors` lookup instead of has+get; `handleRetry` sets the retry error instead of throw-then-catch; the composer's local recovery fence derives from one predicate across components; the queue strip shares `retryBlockedMutation`'s snapshot refusal predicates.
- **Skipped (2):** reading the queue-strip decision from the projection instead of the second direct `readMutationPersistence` (that read's freshness and index are the pinned settle-window behavior, tracked by #1723); and splitting `resumeStopBaseline`'s dual form (the closure reads clearer as-is).

Gates at `298d8ac68` (restacked via `1224eecb8`): `npx biome check --write` exit 0, targeted suites 710/710, `make test-web` exit 0 (typecheck, unit, lint). Zero test-file edits in the pass.

## Round on the 298d8ac finding (1 Medium)

- **Ended-session Send used the narrow fence (was Medium, two reviewers):** the rendered Send's disabled expression was gated on `recoveryFencedLocal` (notLoaded-only) while `availabilityFor` fences every non-active status, so a `closed` session with a restart-blocking obligation and `send: true` (reachable: forceStop sets the obligation, the hub stamps closed frames with Send) rendered an enabled Send that could only toast. The rendered Send now gates on `isLocalRecoveryFenced`, the shared broad predicate `availabilityFor` derives from (`bbde8e13b`). Red-first: "a fenced closed local session that advertises send renders a disabled Send" (failed pre-fix at the disabled assertion).

## Verification

- At `bbde8e13b`: `make test-web` exit 0 (typecheck, unit tests, biome) on the merged tree; targeted suites 691/691.
- At `3fa51902b`: `make test-web` exit 0 (typecheck, unit tests, biome) on the merged tree; targeted suites 648/648 (+54 integration) before the full gate.
- At `fee4eb874`: `npx biome check --write` exit 0 on touched files; targeted suites green (threads 316/316, humanNoteDrafts 22/22, Session 91/91); `make test-web` and CI run on the pushed head.
- At `d7d4c627a`: `make test-web` exit 0 (typecheck, unit tests, biome) on the merged tree; new red-first test "a Stop on the resumed identity during the resume reconnect cancels the resume" (fails on the pre-fix tree).
- Restacked on `origin/main` via merge `89a19ba7f` (no conflicts; the composer contenteditable landing from #1410 required no test changes this round); the descope is commit `c9dd0fd5d` on top. `make test-web` exit 0 (typecheck, unit tests, biome) on the merged tree.
- `npx biome check --write` on every touched file under `cmd/evener-hub/frontend/src` and `appwire-client/typescript` exit 0.
- Mechanism removal verified by inspection and by the acceptance numstat: deletions confined to the cancellation mechanism and its tests; no `canceledMutationIds`, `recordCanceledMutations`, `stoppedSinceBaseline`, or `checkStopped` anywhere in the tree; `restoreProvenAbsent` is back to its two-argument signature in storage, dispatcher, and caller.
- New behavior tests, green: "a fenced stopped local session that advertises send renders a disabled Send" (Composer, fails on the pre-fix tree), "a throwing beforeRequest sends no resume RPC, releases the resume, and keeps the primary ready" (real AppWire client over FakeSocket), "releasing a ref prunes its Stop generation, and a fence captured before the release still fires" (fails on the pre-fix tree).
- The background-note dispatch guard test's previously vacuous wait now proves itself: it asserts the unrelated pending send is not dispatched by the save, then advances the discovery-scan boundary to show the same detector catching the scan's own (legitimate) resend.
- Browser verification is unchanged from before: all six browser guards still time out at their shared navigation boundary before assertions, with no timeout or assertion weakened.

## Related PRs

- #1390: lifecycle logging (merged)
- #1391: isolated restore/Close optimization (merged)
- #1392: completion-aware Resume and cancellation safety; needed for giant-session recovery to complete beyond the ordinary 30-second budget
- Follow-up (planned): durable Stop cancellation of pending outbox sends — `canceled` as an outbox record state, written at user intent before the stop action; carries the restored invariant test.

No live deployment or Resume was performed.

## Known limits

- Sending to a stopped session is refused with the recovery notice rather than resuming. That is a real behavior change against the original promise of this PR, and it is the price of removing the race class rather than fixing it one finding at a time.
- Stop does not take back pending sends (same as `main`); the durable cancellation lands in the follow-up PR.
- The dispatcher admission removal means a fresh Send admitted past an older blocked Send can still stall behind it until the machinery change lands.

prs.title: fix(hub): make explicit Resume completion-owned and cancellable
prs.body:
## Scope

An explicit Resume on a giant session must wait for a real restore instead of being abandoned at the ordinary startup budget, and cancelling it must be safe.

- An explicit `thread/resume` awaits completion, child exit, or caller/Stop cancellation rather than guessing a duration. Heartbeat health checks stay active; the ordinary RPC, automatic-resume, and fresh-spawn budgets are unchanged.
- A Stop or a disconnect cancels that wait and coordinates with actual child reaping, so a Stop cannot report success over a child that is still alive.
- Alias acquisition in context-aware paths uses `LockContext(ctx)` and releases exactly the prefix it acquired, so a cancelled or disconnected request is not left blocked behind a long resume.
- The destruction paths honour cancellation: a cancelled or deadline-expired session delete or project delete fails rather than answering success-with-skip.
- Prelaunch cancellation diagnostics are retained when a candidate log is cleaned up.
- The confirmed-stopped shortcut rechecks the deletion fence for every alias in the group, and refreshes the roster, inputs, and attention notifications before returning success.

## What this PR deliberately does not do

An earlier revision of this branch also carried a chain of **durable exit-proof** mechanisms: a persisted launch-intent marker with startup reconciliation, a persisted signal-intent marker, a retirement-path launch guard, two recovery-state format version bumps, and the durable launch-path invalidation and restoration of a prior owner's exit proof. That whole chain has been removed from this PR and will be designed separately.

The reason is the review history. Each element of that chain was added to answer a finding about the previous one, and the third review round still returned findings on it. The deepest one says the marker approach is itself unsound: recovery settles a group merely because no rendezvous claim exists, so a hub crash after a child started but before it published its claim leaves a live child whose way to a replacement is cleared. That is a design question about where the authority for "this process is gone" comes from, and it does not belong in this PR.

Removed here, and carried by the separate change: the `launch_pending` and `signal_attempted` fields, `recoverInterruptedLaunches` and its startup wiring, `MarkForceStopSignaled`, the retirement-path `LaunchGuard`, and now also `beginLaunchProofLocked` / `restoreLaunchProofLocked`, `BeforeLaunch`'s durable clear, the settle-path restoration, the `proofSettled` / `proofErr` / `ActiveResume.proof` bookkeeping, and the tests that covered them.

Three consequences worth stating plainly:

- The recovery-state file is **unchanged** by this PR: it still writes version 3 with no additional fields. There is no format migration and no downgrade hazard.
- `main` has no launch-path invalidation at all — no `BeforeLaunch`, no proof helpers. This PR now simply stops adding one, so nothing on this path is a regression against `main`.
- The mid-launch crash window that the invalidation would have introduced is **gone with it**. It is not deferred; it does not exist in this branch. Closing it properly is the separate design change's job.

## Tests that moved with the removed mechanism

- `TestActiveResumeProofPersistenceFailures` (`cmd/evener-hub/internal/hubcore/resumelocks_resume_test.go`) — removed entirely. Its subject *is* the invalidation.
- The recreated-hub block of `TestLongRunningResumeFailedCleanupRetainsOwnership` (`cmd/evener-hub/resume_lifetime_test.go`) — three assertions, all of which assert the invalidation's effect across a hub recreation. That test's retained-ownership assertions are unchanged and still pass.
- `TestActiveResumeReapedCleanupPreservesRecoveryAuthority` — **not touched**. It exercises kept behaviour (retained ownership after a failed cleanup, the Stop epoch advancing, a fresh Resume being refused) and passes unchanged. An earlier revision of this description claimed it depended on the invalidation; that claim was wrong, and the test file does not appear in this commit's diff at all.

## What `BeforeLaunch` keeps

Red-first: `TestProjectDeleteRetryCanceledAfterOwnershipReportsError`. The destructive-cleanup/ownership sites were enumerated (`sessionDelete`, both `projectDelete` paths, `resumeProjectDeletions`, `forceStopThread`, `confirmedStoppedWithoutClaim`, `retireDaemon`); this was the only missing guard.
- **Force-stop deletion/cancellation ordering (was Medium):** the confirmed-stopped shortcut takes the per-alias reservations before cancelling when they are free, so its authoritative deletion re-check runs under them before any Resume is aborted; and the verified-process path in `forceStopThread` now does the same at its admission-fence block — all deletion validation under the per-alias reservations completes before `cancelActiveResumes`, because deletion publication takes the same reservations. A clarifying comment now records that at the re-check site.

Red-first: `TestForceStopValidatesSiblingDeletionUnderReservationFallback`.

Red-first: `TestShutdownRechecksCleanupUnderOwnership`.

- **Expected-daemon identity rechecked after cancellation (was Medium):** the confirmed-stopped path now verifies the current rendezvous identity immediately BEFORE `BeginActiveResumeStop`/`cancelActiveResumes`, so a replacement claim in that window refuses the request without aborting the in-flight Resume; the later ownership recheck is retained. Red-first: `TestForceStopConfirmedStoppedRechecksIdentityBeforeCancelingResume`.
- **Confirmed-stopped shutdown fast path skipped the roster refresh (was Low):** it now refreshes before returning success, matching the force-stop shortcut. Red-first: `TestShutdownConfirmedStoppedRefreshesRoster`.

- **Identity validation not atomic with cancellation (was Medium):** the expected-daemon identity is now revalidated under the `BeginForceStop` admission fence, after the reservation attempt and immediately before `cancelActiveResumes`. The atomicity claim, stated in the commit message: with every alias reservation held, no Resume is mid-launch and the fence refuses new admissions, so no Resume-originated claim can appear between check and cancellation. The fallback path's disclosed pre-discovery window is explicitly outside the claim and stays subject to the authoritative post-ownership reread. Red-first: `TestForceStopRevalidatesIdentityUnderFenceBeforeCancelingResume`.

prs.title: Persist round diagnostics for complete transcript replay
prs.body:
Context compaction can make round diagnostics move or duplicate when a client reloads: live projection assigns them to the active logical turn, while persisted checkpoint/summary and copied recovery history can change replay grouping and coordinates.

Persist the logical owner and durable context-compaction presentation records, then use that owner consistently for timing, compaction, hook and steering projection. Mark copied recovery-tail records so model resume retains them while visible transcript, indexed/item paging and ATIF output avoid double-counting. Bump the transcript index version so existing sidecars rebuild with the new grouping rules. Durable write failures do not publish unpersisted compaction announcements.

**Depends on #1098 (environment replay), whose implementation is included in this branch.** The target is main so the repository CI (which only runs for main-targeted PRs) can qualify the current head. Land #1098 first; the diff then contracts to the compaction/timing work. #1110 merged into this branch, not main. #1129 preserves an additional late-owner paging regression now cherry-picked here and is closed as superseded.

The implementation head `0250b5e31701973d8da38dda475b07a442a51d61` includes the queued-mutation rollback prerequisite and the late-owner regression. Focused server/projector/transcript tests pass; its full canonical gate completed with exit 0. The earlier `34ce` canonical gate and CI passed. Those results do not qualify this new head.

Validation at 34ce: real Session/scripted-provider regressions for compaction with a later turn active, the prior turn finished/idle, and PreCompact-hook steering, followed by another ordinary input. Full and one-item live/cold comparisons cover payload, owner, key and position. Focused server/projector/apptranscript normal and race runs both pass. The previous 9cfee CI failure was missing the environment prerequisite; expected coordinates were not weakened. Durable write failure, recovery-copy, ATIF and settlement regressions are included; `make generate` passed on the implementation before prerequisite integration.

Still draft: finish the current full canonical gate and obtain fresh current-head CI/RoboRev after the base-target correction. Current published head `5da490c7f735df57b3fa90193acf54020b7a9021` now includes the latest main and environment prerequisite; its push triggers the previously missing CI. The local canonical run still exercises 0250, so retain that head distinction. Independently review late owner fragments and concurrent fold publication; finish all affected broad gates before merging. Full continuation and recovery instructions: #1116. Higher-level SDK state extraction and the old Tauri app are outside this change.


## Review round 13

Head `9000bc08d` (three fixes plus a merge of main at `0acebbb0d`).

- **Late fragment captured the running turn** (`e489e5da4`). A metadata record
  for a turn that is already over — a fold's compaction record arriving after
  the next turn opened — started a group, and the next assistant or tool record
  joined *that* group instead of the turn still running. The group a
  continuation joins is now tracked apart from the group most recently opened,
  in both the full read and the bounded index, through one shared predicate; a
  delayed steering carrier stays exempt because it does own what follows it.
  The turn-index version is bumped so cached sidecars rebuild.
- **Marker-dependent effects after a failed marker write** (`15beb088b`). Not
  every failed append poisons the writer — a write that transferred no bytes
  leaves it usable — so a fold whose marker write failed still emitted its
  compaction event, named the session from the marker and injected task-list
  steering, with no anchor on disk. The write outcome now gates those effects
  where they all run, matching the rule withheld markers already follow.
- **Replay copies inflated aggregate totals** (`ff9fe20b9`). The usage, derived
  and failed-tool scans counted a fold's copies as real entries, so a session
  was charged twice for the same round and the gap grew with every fold. One
  shared rule now excludes copies from the figures while still reading them for
  tool-name resolution.
- **`RoundTimings.ToolDefs` (Low): refuted.** `allToolDefinitions` returns the
  cached slice built at init (`agent/session_tools.go:1209-1211`), so no
  tool-definition construction happens in the system-prompt window and nothing
  is misattributed. The field is structurally zero because the phase it names
  costs nothing; no falsifiable test exists for assigning it, so it is left
  alone.


## Review round 14

Head `951f8fa24` (four fixes plus a merge of main at `d7ff88653`).

- **#1200, the preserved suffix dropped after a restart: deliberately not in
  this PR.** Diagnosed in full earlier in this review: a fold's copies are the
  PERSISTED forms of pairs appended since its own snapshot, and the preserved
  window is older than that, so closing it needs a durable per-entry identity
  or a marker-side list of the entries its anchor keeps — a transcript format
  change, >150 lines, affecting every session already on main. It lands as its
  own PR immediately after this one: https://github.com/prime-radiant-inc/evener/issues/1200
- **A self-minted turn name outliving its turn** (`2c43213f0`). The name was
  dropped by the follow-up loop, so it ended only for turns that loop finishes;
  any other path left it standing and `activeTurnOwner` prefers it, handing the
  next turn's timing, hook and compaction records — and anything a fold writes
  while idle — to a turn that was over. The turn now ends its own name on every
  path out of `processOneInput`. An interrupted turn keeps it one record
  longer: the marker saying it was cut short belonged to nobody and now belongs
  to the turn it interrupted, in the entry and in the live event.
- **Fold steering announced after its write failed** (`0048bcd96`). The one
  place this series still broke its own write-before-announce rule. The model
  keeps that steering either way — the fold appended it to live history before
  publishing — so the warning reports the divergence and no client is shown a
  line a reload cannot reproduce.
- **A late timing record classified as a carrier** (`e6778c358`). A round's
  timings describe a round that is over, like a compaction record; only
  steering carries the flow. The turn-index version is bumped again because the
  classification moves group boundaries a cached sidecar recorded.


## Review round 15

Head `46f4dd547` (three fixes plus a merge of main). **The turn-index version
did not move: it stays at 18.**

- **Marker-dependent effects asked the anchor question in pieces**
  (`83185f4d6`). A withheld marker suppressed its own event and the fold's
  steering, a failed marker write suppressed only its event, and the transcript
  reminder asked nothing — so a fold whose replay copies landed and whose
  marker write then failed still published its guidance for a compaction a
  reload cannot find. The question is answered once now, where the marker write
  returns, and the compaction event, the session name, the fold's steering and
  the reminder all read that one answer. A fold that writes no marker is
  untouched.
- **Full read and indexed reader disagreed on one owner combination**
  (`77fb6a798`). After a fragment for an earlier turn, metadata owned by the
  turn still running is that turn resuming, and its next record belongs in the
  group that metadata opened — which the indexed reader already said and the
  full read did not. Only the full read changed, so nothing a sidecar records
  moved and the version stays at 18; the batching concern raised last round
  therefore does not come due here.
- **The self-minted name asked the context instead of the outcome**
  (`fece8f69b`). A turn that finished and returned nil under a cancelled
  context kept its name, with no interrupt marker left to claim it. The rule is
  now named and driven directly by its test, since the race it closes cannot be
  forced through the public path.


## Review round 16

Head `7130dbeae` (three fixes plus a merge of main at `42d27f946`, shared
session notes #1070). **The turn-index version moved: 18 → 19.**

- **A fold's two markers now land, and are judged, apart** (`c86e94de6`). A
  checkpoint and a summary reach the transcript independently; one answer for
  the whole fold let a failed checkpoint suppress the effects of a summary that
  IS in the file — the compaction a returning reader anchors on — leaving the
  session unnamed and its guidance unsent. Each record's effects follow its own
  result; the fold's steering and its transcript reminder ask the separate
  question they actually need, whether a reader coming back finds an anchor at
  all. `compactionTurnWithheld`, written and never read, becomes that
  per-record result rather than being deleted.
- **A closed group could be reopened on resume** (`9db0f91f3`). A record's
  persisted turn id is never empty, so the bounded reader's walk back through
  an indexed prefix read an *unowned* checkpoint as a fragment, stepped over
  it, and named the records after it for an opener that checkpoint had ended —
  the same logical turn twice, with different transcript keys, disagreeing with
  the full read. The walk now stops where the flow stopped. **Index version 19**
  because a sidecar written by the old walk holds those names; this is the
  second bump in three rounds, which is the batching cost noted last round.
- **The doctor read a round boundary from a presentational record**
  (`c73b4b06c`). A round's timings or a compaction record between a tool call
  and its result made the result look like it crossed a boundary, and the whole
  archive was refused. Both join the kinds native history already permits
  inside a pending round.

**Merge conflicts with #1070, and how each was resolved** (both intents kept):

- `agent/session_lifecycle.go` — main's notes-projection comment and
  `maybeAppendNotesContext` call at turn start, kept together with this
  branch's `delegatePreseededTurnID` naming of the preseeded turn.
- `agent/session_namer.go` — main's `resetNotesProjectionAfterCompaction()`
  before the compaction-turn event, and this branch's `OwningTurnID` on that
  event.

prs.title: fix(prompt): scope workspace cleanup to deliverables and pin the rule (#302)
prs.body:
## Summary

Scopes the agent-identity workspace-cleanup rule so it can no longer delete agent-built deliverables, and pins the new rule with a regression test. The old rule — "Leave the workspace clean. Remove scratch files, debug scripts, and temporary artifacts you created as soon as you're done with them." — made no distinction between transient scratch and the task's deliverables, so a literal-minded agent could clean up the very thing it was asked to produce (issue #302's own data shows a scored trial where exactly this happened).

Closes #302.

## Root cause

The identity prompt's cleanup rule keyed only on authorship ("you created"), not on handoff state. The issue's counterexample trial (portfolio-optimization, u5nPEMv) deleted `build/`, `__pycache__`, and a compiled `.so` at task end and scored zero, with the interviewed agent reasoning they were "generated artifacts, not source deliverables" — both counterweights then in the prompt failed to prevent it.

## What changed

`agent/prompts/sections/identity.md` — the unscoped rule is replaced by three rules:
1. **Hand back the state the task asked for** — anything the task asked to produce or leave working (file, build output, compiled/installed artifact, running service, deployed config) is the deliverable, not clutter. Never remove or tear it down.
2. **Remove only transient scratch** — scoped to artifacts that are neither part of any deliverable nor needed to rebuild/rerun/verify one. When unsure, leave it in place and say so.
3. **Hand off every deliverable at task end** — name it in the report with its path and how to verify it.

`agent/section_resolver_test.go` — new `TestIdentitySection_CleanupRuleScopedToDeliverables` pins the rule text: positive substrings for all three rules plus a negative assertion against the old unscoped phrasing, so a silent revert to the old wording fails the suite. The test was proven red-first (it fails with 4 assertion errors against the pre-fix identity.md).

## Honest limits (recorded per review)

- A prose rule is still prose: the deliverable classification ultimately keys on the model's judgment of what the task asked for. The new rules close the demonstrated failure mode (build outputs and verification artifacts as deliverables by default; unsure → leave in place), but behavioral validation against the failing task shape is a maintainer decision — the pin test guards the rule text, not model behavior.
- The handoff rule deliberately duplicates a briefer rule in communicate.md.tmpl (belt-and-suspenders on a demonstrated failure mode; noted in the commit).

## Testing

- `go test ./agent/` full package: PASS.
- New pin test verified red-first against the pre-fix wording (4 assertion errors) and green post-fix.
- `make vet`, `make lint`: PASS.

## Review

Two-round adversarial review converged: round 1 found the missing pin (major — the fix was initially completely unpinned; a silent revert would have passed every gate) and wording nits; round 2 verified all closures with independent red-first reproduction, zero findings.

prs.title: Consolidate accreted prompt doctrine; add the oracle-independence pre-flight
prs.body:
## What this is

A reviewed replacement for eight prompt sections under `agent/prompts/sections/`:
`verification.md`, `identity.md`, `workflow.md.tmpl`, `delegation.md`,
`background-jobs.md`, `communicate.md.tmpl`, `tools.md.tmpl`,
`context-management.md.tmpl`. Every other section is untouched.

Two things happen at once. The set is **consolidated** -- the doctrine had
accreted a rule per incident, and merging the duplicates and cutting the dead
weight buys -17% (5025 -> 4177 words). Then verification spends 523 of that
back on **one new block**: the oracle-independence pre-flight. Net -5.4%.

The diff against `main` is large because main does not carry the eval-stack
doctrine commits. The PR's diff is the entire prompt set under test, not an
incremental edit.

## The field evidence

**Rules that are present and inert (#367).** Across 9+ RCA'd trials the agent
recited, verbatim and unprompted, the exact rule that would have prevented its
failure -- when asked afterwards. The doctrine was in the prompt at decision
time and it did nothing. That is the whole argument for the new block not being
another rule.

What it is instead: a per-check act performed *before* the check runs -- name
one specific wrong implementation this check would catch. If nothing comes, or
the only answer is "if it crashed", the check is decoration. Under it, a
nine-row table pairing the rationalization an agent actually reaches for with
what the move really does:

| Thought | Reality |
|---|---|
| "I'll re-derive the value in the check and compare." | You applied your own rule twice and got your own answer twice. |
| "I'll write a second checker in another language." | A different language changes the spelling of the premise, not the premise. |
| "The assertion is fine, the pairing must be wrong." | The pairing *is* the assertion. |

(...and six more.) A rationalization is recognizable in the moment in a way a
principle is not. That is the bet, and it is worth naming before it lands: this
set is close to a wash on volume and is betting entirely on the table earning
its place. The table is also the first markdown table in the assembled prompt --
the right form for a rationalization list, but a form novelty.

**Three residue-rule casualties (#358).** The run-residue rule told an agent to
account for and clear what earlier runs left behind before finishing. It took
three deliverables with it. The rule is deleted. Its one survivor -- flush
incrementally, because a program that only speaks at exit says nothing when it
is interrupted -- folds into workflow's mechanics opener. Identity's
leave-the-workspace-clean bullet now carves out the evidence: *a held-out case
or a reference you built to check your own result is evidence rather than
clutter until the work is reported.* Without that carve-out the new table's rows
6 and 7 tell an agent to build both artifacts and the unscoped cleanup rule
tells it to delete both before reporting.

**Copy-aside vs. the named path (#340).** "Copy the input aside before you touch
it" and "a path the task names is the working location, not an install target"
read together as license to work elsewhere and install back, stranding the build
tree. The copy is now scoped in its own sentence: a shield for one input, not a
new workspace.

**Independence stated twice.** Workflow's "use primary inputs or a check
independent of the construction logic" is gone. Independence now lives in
exactly one place, in verification (#346).

## Test cleanup

Ruling applied: prose-pin assertions die; heading, tool-name, and template-gating
mechanics stay. A prose pin asserts that a particular sentence appears verbatim
in a shipped section -- it reddens on a reflow, it cannot tell a strengthened
rule from a deleted one, and it makes every prose edit a test-maintenance chore.

Every pin was inventoried mechanically (walk each `agent/*_test.go` string
literal of 4+ words, report the ones that appear verbatim inside a shipped
section body), then dispositioned one at a time. Each survivor is re-expressed
as the mechanical fact underneath it: a tool name, a section heading, a typed
identity token (`dlg_...` / `job_...`), or a tracked resolver source.
